Neural Horizons AI | Friday AI Roundup

The Agents Went Shopping. The Bottleneck Is Still Inside Your Company.

Black Friday is here, and some of the shoppers are agents. They are in the cart. They are not in charge of it. Here is what moved this week and what to do about it.

27 NOVEMBER 2026 • WEEKLY AI ROUNDUP • UAE | GLOBAL
01 | Agents go shopping

Agents are shopping. Platforms decide who gets in.

On 24 November Walmart opened its Black Friday deals to Meta’s Muse agent. Amazon is still blocking the same agent.

Shoppers using Muse on Walmart can set spending limits, require approval before a purchase and review every agent-placed order. Muse cannot see their Walmart shopping history. The experience runs on Walmart’s Agent Gateway, which launched in October, and Walmart plans to open it to more AI platforms.

Amazon blocked Muse in September. Reported talks to lift the block are stuck on advertising revenue and on who controls which products the agent recommends. Amazon’s advertising business is worth $68.6 billion a year. That is what it is protecting.

One analytics firm says Muse accounts for 51% of agentic orders. It has not published its method, so treat the number as a direction, not a fact.

Signal: Every retailer now has an agent policy. Most have not written it down. Allow, block or negotiate. Pick one on purpose.

→ Decide which agents may browse, quote and buy from you.

→ Keep product, price and stock data accurate and machine-readable.

→ Expect platform access to become a commercial negotiation.

02 | Adoption

Adoption stalls inside the company. Not in the tool.

A study published on 23 November found the blockers to AI value are mostly organisational.

58 US companies interviewed, across 66 interviews.
~300 AI applications classified by the researchers.
2 in 3 companies reported reduced hiring because of AI, mostly through roles not backfilled.

Source: “Working with AI”, Anthropic, 23 November 2026.

Most gains were more output, not lower cost. Layoffs were rare. The blockers were not technical. Experts resisted deployment. Work that AI does not speed up, such as code review, sales and strategic decisions, became the bottleneck. Adoption was uneven across teams. And people struggled to review the volume of AI output.

Caveat: the findings are qualitative and self-reported, and every company was a customer of the lab that ran the study. Anthropic makes the Claude models. Read it as a pattern, not a measurement.

Signal: Faster output without faster review is a queue, not a gain.

→ Measure your review capacity before you add more AI output.

→ Find the tasks AI does not speed up. Those set your real pace.

→ Bring the experts in early. Resistance is information.

Read the study →
03 | Accountability

Someone must own the agent. Regulators now say it plainly.

On 24 November the UK’s financial regulator published its expectations for agentic AI.

Responsibility stays with the firm and its senior managers, even when a third party supplies the system. Firms should plan how to verify they are dealing with an agent, manage consent, define what an agent may do, and assess liability before accepting payments an agent instructs.

The research points the same way. A new study found that changing the software that runs a model, the harness, moved agent performance by nearly 10 percentage points. The model was not the only variable. Amazon also reported that an open-source agent mostly autonomously exploited a previously unknown vulnerability. And Axios reported that more than two dozen sources say staff at OpenAI and Anthropic worry about releasing some advanced models safely.

Signal: The control layer is now the product. Permissions, limits, logs and an owner.

→ Name one accountable owner per agent.

→ Give every agent a defined scope, a spend limit and an audit trail.

→ Test the harness, not just the model.

Read the FCA page →
04 | AI cyber attacks

Attacks now take hours, not weeks. Patch cycles have not caught up.

<3 hrs Reported time for attackers using ARTEX to reach privileged network access, per the FBI advisory of 13 November.
40+ groups that have targeted UAE infrastructure, according to the head of UAE Government Cyber Security on 18 November.

Sources: FBI flash advisory as reported by Let’s Data Science and CDO Magazine; Khaleej Times, 18 November 2026.

The FBI warned on 13 November about ARTEX, an open-source, AI-driven platform that attackers use to automate intrusions from reconnaissance to data theft.

It was built for authorised security testing. Forks and a commercial version keep it in circulation. This week brought the fallout. The US Treasury’s financial crimes unit took systems offline after unauthorised access, hours after a reported intrusion at the CIA, NGA and ODNI, where investigators suspect ARTEX was repurposed. That link is reported, not confirmed. Todoist also confirmed a breach that began with stolen credentials.

In the UAE, the head of the government’s Cyber Security Council said AI is being used to build attacks and can also find unknown vulnerabilities.

Signal: Attack speed has collapsed from weeks to hours. Patch cycles have not.

→ Treat agent access like privileged access.

→ Rotate and review credentials. Stolen logins still start the chain.

→ Rehearse a three-hour incident, not a three-week one.

05 | Money and machines

Quick hits. The week in five lines.

→ The US FCC approved SpaceX’s plan for up to one million satellites to run AI computing in orbit. The approval covers a potential network. Scientists question the economics and heat dissipation.

→ New US export rules reportedly led lenders to pause billions of dollars in financing tied to major Chinese cloud providers.

→ OpenAI is merging ChatGPT usage limits across Chat and Work. Heavy users of both may hit limits sooner. Wider rollout comes in December.

→ Anthropic says it moved its Messages API from Python to Rust using agents under human review, with about 70% less CPU per request. The figures are company-reported.

→ New York banned AI-chatbot toys for five years.

06 | The UAE

Government goes agentic. And sets a date.

On 25 November the UAE Cabinet approved what it calls the world’s first comprehensive government strategy for agentic AI.

It targets agentic AI across 50% of government operations, services and procedures. The Cabinet also endorsed FedAI, a unified, secure and sovereign ecosystem for building and running agentic AI across federal entities, and told federal bodies to integrate their services with Mira on approved timelines.

Mira, the government concierge agent announced on 23 November, reaches federal-service users from March 2027. It starts with work permits, passports, healthcare and education. It will not only answer questions but process tasks on a user’s behalf. The strategy also covers training 80,000 federal employees in agentic AI.

On the demand side, about half of MENA consumers say they are comfortable with an agent shopping for them (UAE: 54%), and privacy is the top barrier, per Checkout.com’s 2026 report. In Saudi Arabia, HUMAIN says its full stack, including a 3-trillion-parameter open-weight model, goes live on 15 December. Its 88% cost-cut claim is the company’s own. No independent benchmark exists yet.

Signal: Government has set the pace and a date. Private-sector readiness is the gap.

Read the Gulf News report →
07 | How businesses need to go

Agents are in the cart. Six moves for Monday.

Access, review, ownership and speed. The technology is moving faster than the operating model around it.

Your agent readiness check0 of 6

Tap each step you already have in place.

  1. Write your agent policy.Which agents may browse, quote and buy from you. Allow, block or negotiate, on purpose.
  2. Make your product and pricing data accurate and machine-readable.Agents read what you publish. Wrong data becomes a wrong order.
  3. Cap every agent that spends.Limits, approval gates and order review.
  4. Name one owner per agent.One person, one name on the register.
  5. Measure review capacity before you add output.If people cannot review it, more output is a queue.
  6. Treat agent access as privileged access, and patch the same day.Stolen logins and unpatched flaws are how attacks start.

Our view at Neural Horizons AI: start with the business problem. Understand the data. Establish readiness. Build around measurable outcomes. AI is one tool. The value comes from what it enables the business to do.

Questions leaders ask

Why are retailers blocking AI shopping agents?

Control of the customer relationship and of advertising revenue. Amazon blocked Meta's Muse agent in September and is reported to be in talks about lifting the block. The sticking points are ad revenue and who controls which products the agent recommends. Walmart took the opposite route on 24 November and opened its Black Friday deals to Muse with spending limits and approval before purchase.

What did the UAE Cabinet approve on 25 November 2026?

A government strategy for agentic AI that targets agentic AI across 50% of government operations, services and procedures, and the FedAI platform for building and running agentic AI across federal entities. Mira, a government concierge agent, reaches federal-service users from March 2027.

What is ARTEX and why did the FBI warn about it?

ARTEX is an open-source, AI-driven platform built for authorised security testing that attackers have repurposed to automate intrusions. The FBI's 13 November flash advisory says it has helped attackers reach privileged network access in under three hours.

What should a business do about AI agents this week?

Write an agent policy, make product and pricing data accurate and machine-readable, cap every agent that spends, name one owner per agent, measure review capacity before adding output, and treat agent access as privileged access.
